cards.title: Default values
cards.body: Give a parameter a default with `=`. When the caller leaves it out, the default is used.
cards.code:
def repeat(word, times=2):
    return word * times


print(repeat("ha"))
print(repeat("ha", 4))

hi.title: Default values
hi.body: Parameter ko `=` se default value do. Agar call karne wala use chhod de, toh default use hota hai.

cards.title: Returning text
cards.body: A function can build a string and return it, ready for the caller to print.
cards.code:
def label(item, price=1):
    return f"{item}: {price} coin"


print(label("apple"))
print(label("melon", 3))

hi.title: Text return karna
hi.body: Function ek string bana kar return kar sakta hai, jise call karne wala print kar sake.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: `repeat("ha", 3)` should give `hahaha`, but gives `haha`. Which line is wrong?

bug.fix: Line 2 always repeats twice and ignores the parameter. Use it: `return word * times`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: `repeat("ha", 3)` se `hahaha` milna chahiye, par `haha` milta hai. Kaunsi line galat hai?
hi.fix: Line 2 hamesha do baar repeat karti hai aur parameter ko ignore karti hai. Use karo: `return word * times`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: The call passes "!", so it replaces the default "*".

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: Call "!" bhejta hai, isliye woh default "*" ki jagah le leta hai.

exercise.prompt: Finish `greet(name, greeting="Hello")` so it returns `<greeting>, <name>!`. The code below prints `greet(name)` and then `greet(name, "Welcome")`.
exercise.promptHi: `greet(name, greeting="Hello")` poora karo taaki woh `<greeting>, <name>!` return kare. Neeche ka code `greet(name)` aur phir `greet(name, "Welcome")` print karta hai.
exercise.starterCode:
def greet(name, greeting="Hello"):
    # return the greeting text
    return ""


name = input()
print(greet(name))
print(greet(name, "Welcome"))

hiddenTests.expectedOutput:
Hello, Mary Jane!
Welcome, Mary Jane!
